mainEntity.name: Is composite bonding a permanent solution for a rotated tooth?

acceptedAnswer.text: Composite bonding is not considered a permanent treatment. It typically lasts between five and ten years, depending on how well the teeth are maintained, dietary habits, and whether any parafunctional habits such as teeth grinding are present. Over time, the resin material may chip, stain, or wear, at which point it can usually be repaired or replaced. Whilst composite bonding can offer a long-lasting cosmetic result, it requires ongoing care and periodic review by a dental professional.

mainEntity.name: Will composite bonding look natural on a rotated tooth?

acceptedAnswer.text: When performed by a suitably qualified clinician, composite bonding can achieve natural-looking results in appropriate cases. The resin material is available in a wide range of shades and translucencies, allowing the dentist to match the surrounding teeth closely. The key factor is ensuring the bonding is shaped proportionately. For very mild rotations, a suitably qualified dentist can reshape the tooth in a way that aims to complement the appearance of the surrounding smile.

mainEntity.name: Does composite bonding require any tooth preparation?

acceptedAnswer.text: One of the advantages of composite bonding is that it is generally minimally invasive. In most cases, little to no removal of natural tooth structure is required, which differentiates it from treatments such as porcelain veneers or crowns. The dentist may lightly condition the tooth surface to help the resin adhere effectively, but this is typically very superficial. Your dentist will explain exactly what to expect during a consultation.

mainEntity.name: Can a slightly rotated tooth cause any dental health problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: In many cases, mild tooth rotation is purely a cosmetic concern and does not affect function or oral health. However, where rotation causes teeth to overlap or creates tight contact points, it can make thorough cleaning more challenging, potentially increasing the risk of plaque build-up, tooth decay, and gum inflammation. If you are finding it difficult to keep a rotated tooth clean, discussing this with your dentist is a sensible step regardless of whether you are considering cosmetic treatment.

mainEntity.name: How do I know whether I need composite bonding or orthodontic treatment?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most reliable way to determine which approach is right for you is through a clinical examination with a qualified dentist. They will assess the degree of rotation, your bite, the health of your gums and bone, and your aesthetic goals to advise which option — or combination of options — is most appropriate. There is no universal answer, as treatment suitability depends entirely on individual circumstances. A consultation is always the recommended first step.

mainEntity.name: How long does a composite bonding appointment take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A composite bonding appointment typically takes between one and two hours, depending on how many teeth are being treated and the complexity of the work involved. The process involves shade matching, surface preparation, application and sculpting of the composite resin, curing with a specialist light, and final polishing. Most patients find the experience comfortable and straightforward, with results visible immediately after the appointment.
